A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UltraFusion research work and contain readable text, equations, tables and figures. v2 ends with references; v3 additionally includes supplementary Sections A–J. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, qualitative fusion results and a user study involving 136 participants and 20 scenes.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds metric scores, fidelity and alignment analyses, three-exposure evaluation and comparisons with inpainting methods.

M1.justification: The described architecture adds a fidelity control branch that injects image features into the VAE decoder through shortcuts, trained with an L1 reconstruction objective. Appendix F also introduces a three-exposure adaptation using a normal-exposure reference and normalized summation of guidance features. The training-synthesis pipeline was already mentioned in v2; its fuller description alone does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds training and evaluation on Kalantari’s dataset with three exposures. The main MEFB, RealHDRV and UltraFusion evaluations and general-fusion application remain. SICE and Vimeo-90K are newly identified training sources, but the PDFs do not establish that they replaced different sources used in v2.

E2.justification: Appendix I adds actual qualitative comparisons with AnyDoor and Stable Diffusion V2 Inpainting, including a pre-aligned ControlNet output followed by inpainting. Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables is unchanged. Appendix G evaluates the existing six comparators with pre-alignment.

E3.justification: v3 adds DeQA-Score, controlled comparisons with pre-aligned RealHDRV inputs, separate synthesis/alignment ablations and a 512 x 512 inpainting comparison. The new fidelity branch has a separate one-million-iteration training stage. Figure 2’s ControlNet setup changes from pre-aligned inputs in v2’s introduction to explicitly lacking pre-aligned data in v3; this is a reported setting revision without evidence of a rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained alignment and decomposition ablations, v3 adds fidelity-branch removal and architecture tests, separates training-data synthesis from inference-time alignment, and tests whether competing methods benefit from pre-alignment. Appendix H adds regional MEF-SSIM maps. These substantially expand evidence about component contributions, comparison fairness and fidelity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the evaluations. The user-study participant count, scene count and voting-rate reporting are retained; v3 introduces no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Every retained numerical entry in Tables 1–3 is unchanged. Added results include UltraFusion DeQA-Scores of 3.881, 3.830 and 3.957 on MEFB, RealHDRV and UltraFusion, respectively; the no-fidelity-branch result of 0.8763 TMQI and 67.36 MUSIQ; and pre-aligned comparator results in Table A1. New qualitative results demonstrate three-exposure fusion and report better detail preservation than the tested inpainting alternatives.

T1.justification: v3 adds mathematical specifications for the fidelity-branch reconstruction objective and the cross-attention mapping in Eq. A1, including its learnable scaling factor. The original warping and luminance-normalization definitions remain unchanged. No theorems, proofs or theoretical guarantees are added.

C1.justification: The headline claims about guided inpainting, nine-stop exposure fusion, motion robustness and the UltraFusion benchmark remain. The introduction expands the stated contributions to include training-data synthesis and fidelity control, and the conclusion adds fidelity preservation to the architectural contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explains VAE-induced texture distortion and the complementary roles of synthesis and alignment. Appendix H attributes lower MEF-SSIM in dark regions to local adjustments that improve transitions. The conclusion newly acknowledges approximately 3.3-second inference for 512 x 512 inputs, while retaining the limitation concerning unreliable highlight reconstruction after occlusion-estimation failures.

D1.justification: v3 supplies substantial missing training information: SICE/Vimeo-90K sources, exposure selection, flow-derived masks and resizing. It adds fidelity-branch training settings, cross-attention implementation, detailed RealHDRV exposure construction and inference timing. The abstract replaces the online-demo statement with a future code/data-release statement; release availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion remains largely unchanged. v3 adds the Vimeo-90K/task-oriented-flow and DeQA-Score references, explicitly credits L-CAD as inspiration for fidelity control, and develops comparisons with already-cited inpainting approaches. Removing a duplicate SAFNet bibliography entry does not remove that research from consideration.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. v3 edits grammar and introductory explanations, expands methodology and ablation subsections, and adds organized supplementary Sections A–J. Contact information, an internship note and acknowledgments are also added, without wholesale rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is revised to show fidelity control, the component-ablation display gains fidelity examples, and new training-synthesis and alignment figures are introduced. Tables 1–2 gain metric columns, Table 3 gains an ablation row, and the supplement adds Figures A1–A8 and Table A1. Existing benchmark displays are largely retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 invokes a training-synthesis pipeline without explaining its construction. v3 substantially closes that reproducibility gap and documents fidelity control, while new ablations and pre-aligned-baseline comparisons make central fidelity and robustness claims more assessable. These are substantial improvements in documentation and evidential support despite unchanged original benchmark scores. The three-exposure and inpainting comparisons remain qualitative, and statistical uncertainty is still unreported.
